comments.body:
```suggestion
        final int patternLength = pattern.length();
```
or simply use `pattern.length()` directly.

```suggestion
            Arguments.of("", "abc", Set.of()), //
            Arguments.of("", "", Set.of()), //
            Arguments.of("a", "b", Set.of()), //
            Arguments.of("abc", "bcd", Set.of()), //
```
And please remove the `//` at the end of each line.

```suggestion
    private static final int CHARS = Character.MAX_VALUE + 1; // Total number of characters in the input alphabet
```
`char` has 16 bits in java. Therefore maybe one could consider using a `Map`-like structure to represent the state transition table.
In fact, separating each one on one line, I think the code is much cleaner to look at, as it separates each test on just one line. Do you really think it's better to see everything in just one line?

Well... I would leave formatting to clang-format and its setup [`.clang-format`](https://github.com/TheAlgorithms/Java/blob/cdb3affdd9ac4b8c7ccf4c55b05f6914bb9e73d6/.clang-format). I fully agree that having each test case in a separate line is more readable. But I would not _fight_ against clang-format by adding `//`. I am sure that it is possible to change the config of it in such a way, that these test cases will appear in different lines.
Please add the suggested test cases. I think that they are quite useful edge cases.
